acceptance.output_evidence: (1) WHAT WAS SYNTHESIZED, AND WHAT A REAL FORWARD COULD CARRY THAT THESE DO NOT. EVERY BYTE of fixtures/graph/ is synthetic and the manifest's own `claim` field says SYNTHESIZED. Nothing was scrubbed from a real specimen, because there is no real specimen: the cell's own fixture row reads 'real forwarded-message/holdings specimens (STILL MISSING -- proof gap)'. What I had to invent, by shape: the delta page envelope (@odata.context / value[] / @odata.nextLink XOR @odata.deltaLink), the 410 syncStateNotFound body, the 429 + Retry-After header, the attachment list envelope (#microsoft.graph.fileAttachment with id/name/contentType/size/isInline), the /$value raw-bytes response, the retained message/rfc822 MIME, and -- most consequentially -- the internetMessageHeaders of a FORWARDED message: X-MS-Exchange-Organization-OriginalTo, X-MS-Exchange-Organization-OriginalSender and an Authentication-Results line carrying spf/dkim/dmarc with header.from. Those three header names ARE the verification path, and whether Opal's actual forwarding arrangement emits them -- or emits Resent-From, or X-Original-Sender, or nothing but a body quote -- is UNMEASURED. The poller tries a closed ordered list and falls back to the retained original MIME, and if none matches it produces NO_ORIGINAL_SENDER -> UNVERIFIED -> quarantine, which is the safe direction (a message is held, never mis-bound) but would mean EVERY message quarantines on day one. THINGS A REAL FORWARD CAN CARRY THAT NO FIXTURE HERE DOES, stated as a list rather than a gesture: (i) NESTED FORWARDS -- advisor forwards to their assistant who forwards to requests@; the outermost OriginalSender is then the assistant and the advisor survives only inside the innermost message/rfc822 part, which my ORIGINAL_MIME fallback reads only ONE level deep. (ii) CALENDAR ITEMS AND OTHER NON-MAIL TYPES -- a delta over a mail folder returns items whose @odata.type is not #microsoft.graph.message (events, meeting responses); my fixtures contain only messages and the poller does not filter on type, so an event would flow into sender verification and quarantine rather than being skipped as not-a-request. (iii) INLINE IMAGES AND SIGNATURE LOGOS -- real mail carries isInline attachments (contentId-referenced logos, tracking pixels); my fixtures set isInline false everywhere, so the poller persists EVERY attachment, which on a real forward means a signature logo lands in the firm's intake prefix beside the holdings workbook. Not wrong, but noisy, and the filter is unwritten because nothing measured told me what to filter. (iv) itemAttachment and referenceAttachment (a OneDrive link rather than bytes) -- /$value does not answer for either. (v) MIME with folded headers, RFC 2047 encoded words, and multiple Received/Authentication-Results lines from a multi-hop path -- my header parser takes the FIRST Authentication-Results and does no unfolding. (vi) A message with no attachment at all, or a holdings table pasted in the BODY. (vii) Non-ASCII display names and filenames -- my filename sanitizer reduces to [A-Za-z0-9._-], which is safe but lossy. (2) WHAT THE GATEWAY INSPECTION SETTLED, AND WHAT IT LEFT OPEN. SETTLED, with citations in ib_s_6_graph_inspection.md: the estate's only Graph implementation is DELEGATED per-user (graph.py's own docstring); Mail.Read exists but only as a delegated SCOPE on the App-2 registration alongside Mail.Send, Mail.ReadWrite and Files.ReadWrite.All; even the two fixed-mailbox endpoints (/otp/fetch, /ms/*) use a server-held delegated token for a NAMED HUMAN, which is a capability bearer in front of a user's token, not an application permission; no ApplicationAccessPolicy exists anywhere in the corpus (unscoped census); no intake credential exists (list-secrets returns only the gateway's two); and the app-only shape was CTO-ruled ONCE, for the BD OTP adapter, and never landed. Therefore the gateway is NOT a reuse source, and reusing its secret would WIDEN a credential carrying send and write scopes to a new consumer. LEFT OPEN, and not closable from inside this order: whether IT will consent Mail.Read (Application) on a new registration; whether an ApplicationAccessPolicy scoping it to opalbloomberg@opalinvest.com will be created; and what the mail flow from requests@opalinvest.com into that mailbox looks like ON THE WIRE -- which is what decides whether the forwarding-header verification above matches reality. All three are acts outside this repository and all three are prerequisites of the first live run. ALSO LEFT OPEN AND NOT ASKED ABOUT: the per-firm execution roles the FirmDestinationPolicy names cannot be assumed by any running function (row IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S3, grounded on the APPLIED plane), so this poller runs under one role narrowed to the intake prefix family rather than becoming each firm's principal. (3) WHAT 'WITHIN A SHORT TIME' (FWD-9 ACCEPT) WOULD MEASURE AS ONCE THE POLLER IS ENABLED. The honest decomposition is FOUR terms, only one of which this cell controls. T1, SCHEDULE LATENCY: 0 to 15 minutes, uniform, from the applied cron(0/15 8-23 * * ? *) America/New_York -- expected 7.5 minutes inside the window. T2, OUT-OF-WINDOW WAIT: a message arriving at 23:50 waits until 08:00 the next day, about 8h10m; this is the brief's own accepted behaviour ('A request received overnight is collected when the daily window resumes'), so a measurement that averaged over the whole day rather than reporting the in-window and out-of-window arms SEPARATELY would report a number that describes neither. T3, MAIL DELIVERY: the time from the advisor's send to the message becoming visible in the delta -- Exchange forwarding plus indexing, typically seconds to a minute, but UNMEASURED here and not ours. T4, SCAN DURATION: fixture-measured only; the Lambda timeout is 120s and the catch-up bound is 50 pages / 500 messages, so a scan that exceeds the bound STOPS WITHOUT ADVANCING THE CHECKPOINT and the next window resumes -- which means a backlog large enough to hit the bound converts T1 into a multiple of 15 minutes, and that is the tail worth stating. SO: a defensible ACCEPT measures 'forward sent -> request_id visible in the portal' at the 50th and 95th percentile, REPORTED SEPARATELY for in-window and out-of-window arrivals, with the denominator being forwards sent rather than requests created (a message that quarantines produces no request and would silently leave the numerator). A single 'within a short time' number over a mixed population would be dominated by T2 and would say nothing about the system. NONE OF THIS IS MEASURABLE TODAY: the schedule is DISABLED, the application permission does not exist, and no forward has ever been read.

mutant.description: The central claim of arms (a) and (c) is that the CONDITIONAL completion mark is what makes a re-read a no-op. Two mutants remove exactly that behaviour and nothing else, by monkeypatch in a process that edits no production file: M1 makes Checkpoint.is_complete always return False (the short-circuit is gone); M2 additionally drops if_absent from the mark's write (the claim is no longer conditional). A passing assertion never mutated has never been tested, and the specific risk here is that a durability suite written by the author of the durability code agrees with itself.
